```{r}
                      "arrow", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "caret", "corrplot", "ck37r",

# Function to install missing packages
install_if_missing = function(package) {
 if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly = TRUE)) {
   install.packages(package)
 }
}

# Install and load each package
for (package in required_packages) {
 tryCatch({
   install_if_missing(package)
   library(package, character.only = TRUE)
 }, error = function(e) {
   message(sprintf("Failed to load package: %s\nError: %s", package, e$message))
 })
}
```

```{r}
# "Missing data were imputed via 5 independent runs of missRanger using predictive mean matching (PMM) with 5 
# nearest neighbors. Each run used 1000 trees per random forest and 5 iterations. 
# For variables with  missingness (e.g., anxiety disorders), final values were determined by modal 
# (categorical) or median (continuous) consensus across runs. 
# PMM ensured imputations reflected observed data distributions while multi-run aggregation was performed to partly account for single-imputation bias."
# ----- IMPUTATION WITH missRanger AND PMM-BASED CONSENSUS -----
# 1. Generate 5 independent imputations using different random seeds
# 2. Aggregate results using median/mode to handle high missingness variables
# 3. Maintain PMM benefits while accounting for extreme imputation values across individual runs 
# Note: Extreme values are less likely within MissRanger at default since 
# First identify columns with missing values since PMM ensures imputed values are drawn from observed data 
missing_cols = colnames(df_indicators)[colMeans(is.na(df_indicators)) > 0]
cat("Columns with missing values:\n")
cat(paste(missing_cols, collapse="\n"), "\n\n")

# Convert categorical columns to factors (if applicable)
df_indicators = df_indicators %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(missing_cols), ~{
    if(is.character(.)) as.factor(.) else .
  }))

# Create formula for missing columns
formula_str = as.formula(paste(paste(missing_cols, collapse = " + "), "~ . - person_id"))
cat("\nFormula:\n")
cat(paste(missing_cols, collapse = " +\n"), "\n~\n. - person_id\n")
```

# Imputing Missing Values
```{r}
# --- Generate 5 Imputed Datasets with Different Seeds across dfs ---
n_imputations = 5
base_seed = 505  # For reproducibility
imputed_datasets = vector("list", n_imputations)
```


```{r}
# Running missRanger imputation with 5 repeats 
# - Predictive Mean Matching (PMM) used maintain realistic values
#### Steps involved for PMM: 
#### 1. Using random forest to predict missing values
#### 2. Finding k nearest neighbors among observed values
#### 3. Randomly selecting one of these neighbors as the imputed value
#### Preserves a) natural distribution of variables, b) valid category levels, c) relationship between variables


for(i in seq_len(n_imputations)) {
  cat(sprintf("\nImputation run %d/%d\n", i, n_imputations))
  
  imputed_datasets[[i]] = missRanger(
      df_indicators,
      formula = formula_str,        # Formula to impute only missing columns    
      pmm.k = 5,                    # Number of nearest neighbors for predictive mean matching
      num.trees = 1000,             # Number of trees per random forest
      maxiter = 5,                  # Maximum number of imputation rounds
      max.depth = 10,               # Maximum tree depth
      min.node.size = 50,           # Minimum leaf size
      sample.fraction = 0.5,        # Fraction of data used per tree
      verbose = 1,                  # Show progress 
      data_only = FALSE             # Returns imputed data and a "missRanger" object with additional info
  )
}
```

```{r}
#' Analyze and Summarize Multiple Imputation Results for a Single Variable
#'
#' This function examines the results of multiple imputation runs for a specified variable,
#' generating consensus values and summary statistics. 
#' Median is used for numeric variables (excluding binary columns) whereas mode is used for factors/binary 
#' @param variable Character string specifying the name of the variable to analyze
#' @param imputed_list List of imputed datasets, where each element contains a data frame
#'                     with the complete (imputed) dataset
#' @param original_df Data frame containing the original dataset with missing values
#'
#' @return List containing four elements:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item raw_imputations: Matrix where rows are missing values and columns are imputation runs
#'     \item consensus_values: Vector of final imputed values for each missing position
#'     \item summary_stats: For numeric variables: list with median, sd, and range
#'                         For categorical variables: frequency table of consensus values
#'     \item imputation_table: Data frame comparing imputations across runs with consensus values
#'   }
#'
inspect_imputations = function(variable, imputed_list, original_df) {
  # Identify positions of missing values in the original dataset for this variable
  na_pos = is.na(original_df[[variable]])
  
  # Create a matrix where each row is a missing value and each column is an imputation run
  imputed_vals = sapply(imputed_list, function(d) d$data[[variable]][na_pos])
  
  # Generate summary statistics based on variable type (numeric vs categorical)
  if(is.numeric(original_df[[variable]])) {
    # For numeric variables: calculate median across imputation runs for each missing value
    consensus = apply(imputed_vals, 1, median)
    # Compute descriptive statistics of the consensus values
    stats = list(
      median = median(consensus),
      sd = sd(consensus),
      range = range(consensus)
    )
  } else {
    # For categorical variables: calculate mode (most common value) across imputation runs
    consensus = apply(imputed_vals, 1, get_mode)
    # Compute frequency distribution of consensus values
    stats = table(consensus)
  }
  
  # Create a combined data frame showing raw imputations and consensus values side-by-side
  imputation_table = as.data.frame(imputed_vals)
  colnames(imputation_table) = paste0("Run_", 1:ncol(imputed_vals))
  imputation_table$Consensus = consensus
  
  # Return a list containing raw imputed values, consensus values, summary statistics, and the comparison table
  list(
    raw_imputations = imputed_vals,    # Matrix of all imputed values across runs
    consensus_values = consensus,      # Final imputed value for each missing position
    summary_stats = stats,             # Summary statistics of consensus values
    imputation_table = imputation_table  # Table comparing each run's imputation with the consensus
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Function to compute mode for categorical variables
compute_mode = function(x) {
  ux = unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

#' Analyze Disagreements Between First Imputation Run and Consensus Values
#'
#' This function evaluates the consistency of multiple imputation results by comparing
#' the first imputation run against the consensus values derived from all runs.
#' It handles categorical, binary, and continuous variables differently and provides
#' detailed statistics about disagreements.
#'
#' @param variable_name Character string naming the variable to analyze
#' @param imputed_datasets List of imputed datasets from multiple runs
#' @param df_original Original dataset containing missing values
#'
#' @return List containing:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item variable: Name of analyzed variable
#'     \item num_disagreements: Count of values where Run 1 differs from consensus
#'     \item total_imputed: Total number of imputed values
#'     \item percent_disagree: Percentage of Run 1 values that differ from consensus
#'     \item consensus_type: Method used for consensus ("Mode" or "Median")
#'     \item disagreement_table: Sample of up to 40 cases where Run 1 differs from consensus
#'   }
#'
calculate_disagreement = function(variable_name, imputed_datasets, df_original) {
 
  # Check for missing values in original dataset
  original_missing = is.na(df_original[[variable_name]])
  if (sum(original_missing) == 0) {
    stop("No missing values found for ", variable_name, " in original data")
  }
  
  # Create matrix of imputed values where each column represents one imputation run
  imputed_values = sapply(imputed_datasets, function(run) {
    run$data[[variable_name]][original_missing]
  })
  colnames(imputed_values) = paste0("Run_", 1:ncol(imputed_values))  
  
  # Determine if variable is categorical or continuous
  is_factor = is.factor(imputed_datasets[[1]]$data[[variable_name]])
  is_numeric = is.numeric(imputed_datasets[[1]]$data[[variable_name]]) 
  is_binary = all(imputed_values %in% c(0,1))
      
  # Compute consensus value for each missing entry based on variable type
  if (is_factor || is_binary) {
     
    # Use mode for categorical or binary variables
    consensus = apply(imputed_values, 1, compute_mode)
    consensus_type = "Mode"
  } else if (is_numeric) {
      
    # Use median for continuous variables
    consensus = apply(imputed_values, 1, median)
    consensus_type = "Median"
  } else {
    stop("Unrecognized type for ", variable_name)
  }
  
  # Compare Run 1 with consensus to count disagreements
  run1_values = imputed_values[, "Run_1"]
  
  # Count how many times Run 1's prediction differs from consensus
  disagreements = sum(run1_values != consensus, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Total number of missing values that were imputed
  total_imputed = length(consensus)
  
  # Calculate what percentage of Run 1's predictions differ from consensus
  percent_disagree = (disagreements / total_imputed) * 100
  
  # Create sample table showing specific instances where Run 1 differs from consensus
  # Find positions where Run 1 disagrees with consensus value
  disagreement_indices = which(run1_values != consensus)
  if (length(disagreement_indices) > 0) {
      
      # Limit to first 40 disagreements for brevity 
      sample_indices = head(disagreement_indices, 40)
      
      # Create a table with Run 1, Consensus, and Runs 2-5 for these sample rows
      disagreement_table = data.frame(
          Consensus = consensus[sample_indices],
          Run_1 = imputed_values [sample_indices, "Run_1"],
          imputed_values[sample_indices, -1, drop = FALSE]
      )
      
  } else {
      disagreement_table = data.frame() # Return an empty data frame if no disagreement 
  }
    
  # Return list of results (including disagreement statistics and sample table)
  list(
    variable = variable_name,
    num_disagreements = disagreements,
    total_imputed = total_imputed,
    percent_disagree = percent_disagree,
    consensus_type = consensus_type,  
    disagreement_table = disagreement_table 
  )
}
```

```{r}
create_consensus_imputation = function(imputed_datasets, df_original) {
  # Initialize consensus dataset
  df_consensus = df_original
  
  # Identify columns with missingness
  missing_cols = names(df_original)[colSums(is.na(df_original)) > 0]
  
  for(col in missing_cols) {
    na_pos = is.na(df_original[[col]])
    num_missing = sum(na_pos)
    
    if(num_missing == 0) next
    
    # Extract imputed values as characters (preserve factor labels)
    imputed_vals = sapply(imputed_datasets, function(d) {
      vals = d$data[[col]][na_pos]
      if(is.factor(vals)) as.character(vals) else vals
    })
    
    # Force matrix structure
    if(!is.matrix(imputed_vals)) {
      imputed_vals = matrix(imputed_vals, nrow = num_missing)
    }
    
    # Apply aggregation
    if(is.factor(df_consensus[[col]])) {
      modes = apply(imputed_vals, 1, compute_mode)
      df_consensus[[col]][na_pos] = factor(modes, levels = levels(df_original[[col]]))
    } else {
      df_consensus[[col]][na_pos] = apply(imputed_vals, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  
  df_consensus
}
```

```{r}
# Applying consensus imputed values within the existing dataframe

# Confirming no missing values 
stopifnot(sum(is.na(df_consensus)) == 0)
str(df_consensus)

# Checking for missing values
```

```{r}
# Using missRanger for imputation of missing values with:
# - Predictive Mean Matching (PMM) used maintain realistic values
#### Steps involved for PMM: 
#### 1. Using random forest to predict missing values
#### 2. Finding k nearest neighbors among observed values
#### 3. Randomly selecting one of these neighbors as the imputed value
#### Preserves a) natural distribution of variables, b) valid category levels, c) relationship between variables


# - Case weights downsample rows with more missing data 
# - 1000 trees used as a trade-off between speed/accuracy
```

```{r}
# Set education 'other' to NA in df_consensus

                               levels = setdiff(levels(df_consensus$education), "other"))
```

```{r}
# Example formula for imputation 
formula_str = as.formula("education ~ . - person_id")

# Example imputation code 
imp_model = missRanger(
  df_consensus,
  formula = formula_str,        # Use all other columns to predict education
  pmm.k = 5,                    # Number of nearest neighbors for predictive mean matching
  num.trees = 1000,             # Number of trees per random forest
  maxiter = 1,                  # Only one iteration needed since we're imputing just one column
  max.depth = 10,               # Maximum tree depth
  min.node.size = 50,           # Minimum leaf size
  sample.fraction = 0.5,        # Fraction of data used per tree
  verbose = 1,                  # Show progress 
  data_only = FALSE             # Return full missRanger object
)
```

# Summary table

```{r}
# Skip custom formula, select relevant columns for propensity matching
# Define confounders by excluding unnecessary columns
confounders = setdiff(names(df_consensus), c("person_id", "gad_completion"))

# Select variables for propensity model
model_vars = c("gad_completion", confounders)
psm_data = df_consensus[model_vars]

# Fit propensity score model
ps_model = glm(gad_completion ~ ., data = psm_data, family = binomial())

summary(ps_model)

```

```{r}
# Wald confidence intervals are based on the idea that the estimator (often the maximum likelihood estimator) 
# is approximately normally distributed. 
# This means the interval is calculated simply as the estimator plus or minus a multiple of its standard error, 
# assuming a symmetric distribution.

params_mb = model_parameters(ps_model, ci_method = "wald", exponentiate = TRUE)

summary_table_wald = params_mb %>% 
  rename(odds_ratio = Coefficient)

print(summary_table_wald)
str(summary_table_wald)
```


```{r}
library(boot)
library(broom)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(parallel)

# Define a bootstrap function that refits the model and returns coefficients
boot_fn = function(data, indices) {
  d = data[indices, ]
  fit = glm(gad_completion ~ ., data = d, family = binomial())
  return(coef(fit))
}

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(280)

# Determine number of cores available
n_cores = detectCores() - 1  # leave one core free

# Perform bootstrapping with 1000 iterations in parallel
boot_results = boot(data = psm_data,
                     statistic = boot_fn,
                     R = 1000,
                     parallel = "multicore",  
                     ncpus = n_cores)

# Compute the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles for each coefficient across bootstrap replications
boot_ci = apply(boot_results$t, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))

# Get the original coefficient estimates and p-values from the model summary
orig_coefs = coef(ps_model)
pvals = coef(summary(ps_model))[, "Pr(>|z|)"]

# Create a summary table
summary_table_boot = data.frame(
  term = names(orig_coefs),
  estimate = orig_coefs,
  odds_ratio = exp(orig_coefs),
  conf.low = exp(boot_ci[1, ]),
  conf.high = exp(boot_ci[2, ]),
  p.value = pvals
)

# Print the table as a tibble for nicer formatting
print(as_tibble(summary_table_boot), n = Inf, width = Inf)
```


```{r}
# Profile likelihood confidence intervals work by “profiling” the likelihood function: 
# for each value of the parameter of interest, they maximize the likelihood over the other parameters. 
# The interval is then defined by the set of parameter values where the likelihood is within a certain threshold 
# relative to its maximum. 
# This method better captures the actual shape of the likelihood, often resulting in asymmetric intervals that 
# can be more accurate, especially when the standard normal approximation (assumed in the Wald method) fails.

# Extract coefficient table 
summary_table = tidy(ps_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
 rename(odds_ratio = estimate) 

# Printing the entire summary_table without truncation
print(summary_table, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```


```{r}
# Install and load the parameters package if not already installed

# Compute model parameters using bootstrapping 
params = model_parameters(ps_model, ci_method = "profile")

# Print the coefficient table with robust confidence intervals and p-values
print(params)
```


```{r}
# Extract coefficient table with parallel processing 

options(future.globals.maxSize = 800 * 1024^2)  # 800 MiB in bytes

# Set up parallel processing (multisession works on Windows/Mac/Unix)
plan(multisession)

# Extract parameter names from the ps_model object
params = names(coef(ps_model))

# Define a function to compute CI for one parameter using profile likelihood
compute_ci = function(param) {
  # confint() returns a 2-column matrix for the given parameter
  ci = confint(ps_model, parm = param)
  return(ci)
}

# Compute confidence intervals for each parameter in parallel
ci_list = future_lapply(params, compute_ci)

# Combine the list into a matrix, ensuring rownames match the parameter names
ci_parallel = do.call(rbind, ci_list)
rownames(ci_parallel) = params

# Get a tidy summary of the model WITHOUT confidence intervals
summary_table = tidy(ps_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = FALSE) %>%
  rename(odds_ratio = estimate)

# Merge in the parallel-computed confidence intervals
# Note: the 'term' column in summary_table must match the rownames of ci_parallel
summary_table = summary_table %>%
  mutate(
    conf.low = exp(ci_parallel[term, 1]),
    conf.high = exp(ci_parallel[term, 2])
  )

# Print the complete summary table
print(summary_table, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

# Response probabilities first iteration
```{r}
# Generate predicted probabilities and weights directly in the dataframe
df_consensus = df_consensus %>%
  mutate(
    response_prob = predict(ps_model, df_consensus, type = "response"),
    observation_wt = 1 / response_prob,
    # Create trimmed versions (only trimming lower bound)
    response_prob_trim = pmax(response_prob, 0.001),
    observation_wt_trim = 1 / response_prob_trim,
    # Add log-transformed weights
    log_observation_wt = log(observation_wt),
    log_observation_wt_trim = log(observation_wt_trim)
  )

head(df_consensus)

# Calculate summary statistics for all metrics
summary_stats_metrics = df_consensus %>%
  summarise(
    # Response probabilities
    prob_min = min(response_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_max = max(response_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_mean = mean(response_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_sd = sd(response_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Trimmed response probabilities
    prob_trim_min = min(response_prob_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_trim_max = max(response_prob_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_trim_mean = mean(response_prob_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    prob_trim_sd = sd(response_prob_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Observation weights
    wt_min = min(observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_max = max(observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_mean = mean(observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_sd = sd(observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Trimmed observation weights
    wt_trim_min = min(observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_trim_max = max(observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_trim_mean = mean(observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    wt_trim_sd = sd(observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Log observation weights
    log_wt_min = min(log_observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_max = max(log_observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_mean = mean(log_observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_sd = sd(log_observation_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Log trimmed observation weights
    log_wt_trim_min = min(log_observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_trim_max = max(log_observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_trim_mean = mean(log_observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_wt_trim_sd = sd(log_observation_wt_trim, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print formatted summary statistics
cat("\nSummary Statistics for Propensity Score Analysis:\n")
cat("================================================\n\n")

cat("Response Probabilities:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.4f to %.4f\n", summary_stats_metrics$prob_min, summary_stats_metrics$prob_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n\n", summary_stats_metrics$prob_mean, summary_stats_metrics$prob_sd))

cat("Trimmed Response Probabilities:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.4f to %.4f\n", summary_stats_metrics$prob_trim_min, summary_stats_metrics$prob_trim_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n\n", summary_stats_metrics$prob_trim_mean, summary_stats_metrics$prob_trim_sd))

cat("Observation Weights:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.2f to %.2f\n", summary_stats_metrics$wt_min, summary_stats_metrics$wt_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.2f (SD: %.2f)\n\n", summary_stats_metrics$wt_mean, summary_stats_metrics$wt_sd))

cat("Trimmed Observation Weights:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.2f to %.2f\n", summary_stats_metrics$wt_trim_min, summary_stats_metrics$wt_trim_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.2f (SD: %.2f)\n\n", summary_stats_metrics$wt_trim_mean, summary_stats_metrics$wt_trim_sd))

cat("Log Observation Weights:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.3f to %.3f\n", summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_min, summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.3f (SD: %.3f)\n\n", summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_mean, summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_sd))

cat("Log Trimmed Observation Weights:\n")
cat(sprintf("Range: %.3f to %.3f\n", summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_trim_min, summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_trim_max))
cat(sprintf("Mean: %.3f (SD: %.3f)\n", summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_trim_mean, summary_stats_metrics$log_wt_trim_sd))
```

```{r}
# First, verify the files are created locally
if (!file.exists(df_consensus_filename) || !file.exists(summary_table_filename)) {
  stop("Local files not created successfully")
}

# Create a function to handle file copying and verification
verify_bucket_copy = function(filename, bucket_path) {
  # Copy file to bucket
  copy_result = system(paste0("gsutil cp ./", filename, " ", bucket_path, "/data/"), intern=TRUE)
  
  # Verify copy was successful
  file_extension = tools::file_ext(filename)
  ls_result = system(paste0("gsutil ls ", bucket_path, "/data/*.", file_extension), intern=TRUE)
  
  # Check if file exists in bucket
  if (!any(grepl(filename, ls_result))) {
    warning(paste("File", filename, "not found in bucket"))
    return(FALSE)
  }
  return(TRUE)
}

# Execute the verification process
tryCatch({
  # Copy and verify summary table
  summary_verified = verify_bucket_copy(summary_table_filename, my_bucket)
  
  # Copy and verify imputed data
  consensus_verified = verify_bucket_copy(df_consensus_filename, my_bucket)
  
  # Print verification results
  if (summary_verified && consensus_verified) {
    message("All files successfully copied and verified in bucket")
  } else {
    warning("Some files may not have been copied successfully")
  }
}, error = function(e) {
  stop(paste("Error in bucket operations:", e$message))
})
```

```{r}
      c(response_prob, observation_wt, response_prob_trim, observation_wt_trim),
      list(
        min = ~round(min(.), 4),
        q1 = ~round(quantile(., 0.25), 4),
        mean = ~round(mean(.), 4),
        median = ~round(median(.), 4),
        q3 = ~round(quantile(., 0.75), 4),
        max = ~round(max(.), 4)
      )
    )
  )

# Function to print formatted statistics for each metric
print_metric_stats = function(name, stats) {
  cat("\n", name, "\n", sep="")
  cat(paste(rep("=", nchar(name)), collapse=""), "\n")
  cat(sprintf("Minimum:  %10.4f\n", stats$min))
  cat(sprintf("Q1:       %10.4f\n", stats$q1))
  cat(sprintf("Mean:     %10.4f\n", stats$mean))
  cat(sprintf("Median:   %10.4f\n", stats$median))
  cat(sprintf("Q3:       %10.4f\n", stats$q3))
  cat(sprintf("Maximum:  %10.4f\n", stats$max))
}

# Print formatted statistics for each metric

cat("==========================================\n")
```

```{r}
# Function for creating density plots
plot_weight_density = function(weights, title) {
  ggplot(data = data.frame(weight = weights), aes(x = weight)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), 
                   bins = 50, 
                   fill = "#7AA6C2",
                   color = "white", 
                   alpha = 0.7) + 
    geom_density(color = "#2C3E50", linewidth = 1) +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Predicted Probability of GAD Assessment Completion",
         y = "Distribution Density") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      text = element_text(family = "sans")
    )
}

# Revised boxplot function with clearer labels
plot_weight_boxplot = function(weights, title) {
  data = data.frame(value = weights)
  
  max_val = max(weights, na.rm = TRUE)
  min_val = min(weights, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = 1, y = value)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "#7AA6C2", 
                 color = "#2C3E50",
                 outlier.color = "#E74C3C",
                 outlier.shape = 16,
                 outlier.size = 2,
                 width = 0.5) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(min_val, max_val)) +
    labs(title = title,
         y = "Predicted Probability of GAD Assessment Completion") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(family = "sans")
    )
}

# Calling plot functions
p1 = plot_weight_density(df_imputed$response_prob, "Distribution of Response Probabilities")
p2 = plot_weight_boxplot(df_imputed$response_prob, "Response Probabilities")

p1
p2
```
